ky_pendergrass_murray_recreational_prese.blurb: This large preserve lies in the southern part of Red River Gorge, Kentucky, with dozens of crags tucked into side hollows such as Coal Bank Hollow and Flat Hollow. Sport climbing dominates, with a good number of trad lines and almost no top-roping or bouldering. The sandstone here is typical of the gorge: cliffs that tend to lean out, with pockets and plate-shaped holds, and some very large caves. Trees shade at least some of the faces, such as The Gallery. Difficulty leans hard, with 5.10 through 5.12 the bulk of the climbing and a real tail up to 5.14, though a modest set of 5.8 and 5.9 routes exists. Drive-By Crag is another of its bigger walls.

vt_bolton_area.blurb: Bolton sits in the Green Mountains of northern Vermont, about half an hour from Burlington. The rock is green schist, which ranges from very solid to rather loose and has a reputation for being hard to read. Bouldering is the largest share, with sport and trad close behind and a few top-ropes. Roped grades run from easy up to 5.13, with 5.10 the most common and a broad middle from 5.7 to 5.11; problems are mostly V0 to V4 with some much harder. Bolton Dome is a south-facing wall that is best in spring and fall because summer sun makes it hot. Bolton Quarry and Lower West are short walks, while Bone Mountain is a long hike in.

co_devil_s_head.blurb: Devil's Head is a granite climbing area in the Rampart Range, part of the South Platte, with views out toward Pikes Peak. The granite is fine and even rather than the coarse crystals common nearby, and it gives roofs, cracks, edges and flakes, so there is more face climbing than usual for the region. Sport is the main style by a wide margin, with a smaller set of trad crack lines and a few multi-pitch routes. Grades center on 5.10 to 5.12, with some 5.9s and a few 5.13s. Crags face south, east and west, and most climbing happens from roughly April through November. Radio Head, Devil's Gate Sector and The Arena are among the bigger sectors.

co_san_luis_valley.blurb: Climbing in the San Luis Valley of south-central Colorado is centered on Penitente Canyon, a small canyon of volcanic welded tuff with good friction, crimps and edges, and walls covered in huecos. Sport climbing dominates, with fewer trad lines and a solid bouldering scene. Most roped routes are 5.10 and harder, with 5.10 to 5.12 the bulk and few easy ones, so it suits those pushing their grades. Problems run from easy to V8 and beyond. South-facing routes can be climbed in any season. Up on Wolf Creek Pass, Big Meadows is a quiet summer spot that turns into the winter ice area, with ice up to about WI5. The Rock Garden and Witches' Canyon sit close to Penitente.

az_flagstaff_bouldering.blurb: Flagstaff sits at nearly 7,000 feet, and its bouldering changes rock from one area to the next. Priest Draw is limestone with pocketed roofs and is the best-known spot; Kelly Canyon is slopey, gymnastic sandstone; the San Francisco Peaks and Mt. Elden give technical, crimpy dacite; and Buffalo Park has columnar basalt with moderate to mid-grade problems. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V6 and a tail of harder lines up to V13. Many areas are in town or a 20 to 30 minute drive away. Priest Draw has sheltered overhangs that allow climbing through nearly the whole year.

ca_tahquitz_suicide_rocks.blurb: Tahquitz Rock and Suicide Rock are granite crags near Idyllwild, a long-established destination for multi-pitch trad. Routes run from one to seven pitches, and nearly everything is traditional; sport lines are uncommon, and even bolted ones can be run out. The granite is good quality, from smooth and nearly featureless to rough and grainy. Grades cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent spread of 5.6 to 5.9 and a few 5.12s and 5.13s. Suicide Rock is the larger of the two, has little loose rock, sits lower, and clears of snow earlier in spring but runs hotter in summer. The north side of Tahquitz has loose rock and should be treated like an alpine face. Climbing generally runs from mid to late spring through mid to late fall.
